clause_evidence.reasoning: Every sample presents data in pictograph form and explicitly requires learners to organize that data by reading each row, counting the pictograph symbols, and transferring the values into a structured table format with category labels and count fields.

All twenty samples employ emoji pictographs as the visual representation of data. Each pictograph uses a consistent emoji symbol repeated horizontally in rows, with row labels identifying the category being represented, which is the essential structure of a pictograph.

None of the samples employ a pictograph scale, meaning no sample contains notation such as one symbol representing two items or other multiplicative relationships. Each pictograph uses one-to-one mapping where a single emoji represents exactly one unit.

Every sample includes a structured table as the target response format. Each table contains a category column with the names of items and a count column with empty cells for learners to fill in. The table structure is consistent across all samples.
